method: Semantic reading of TensorResolventScalarsR4 and CanonicalTensorResolventR2 followed by full R2/R3 diff inspection; existing receipt/axiom/olean/source hashes verified. No independent rebuild.
findings: Product B/A=exp(-c sum(xi)) is proved inductively; hence the resolvent multiplier is sigmoid(2c sum(xi)), not an unjustified tensor identity A²+B²=I.
The scalar coefficient A_product²+B_product² is strictly positive pointwise. Cancellation is applied almost everywhere to vector values; it does not assert a bounded inverse for that coefficient.
Q intertwines the actual Fock resolvent with the scalar multiplier as a proved equation. The bounded-intertwiner theorem then transports its damping-defined imaginary powers.
The phase sign matches the existing conventions: sumEnergy=-2c sum(xi), c=-2pi²; the boost parameter is -2pi t, and characterPhase contributes its own negative sign.
The conclusion is for every sector n+1 of the unchanged Fock. The vacuum sector n=0 remains outside this theorem and must be composed separately for a full operator equality.
R3 changes relative to the reviewed R2 are namespace/coercion elaboration and explicit equality composition; no conclusion is inserted as a new hypothesis.
scope_limits: This receipt verifies the positive-sector BW identity only; the full Fock equality requires the separately handled vacuum sector.
No KMS strip analyticity, scalar dual-weight modular implementation or scaled trace is proved by these two sources.
